explanation: Existing PR #3 visitor explanation was rechecked directly against museum catalog, official scholarship or artist's letter. Existing database facts/curation/emotions/rights remain unchanged; Met says the Saint-Rémy countryside composition was painted on the spot; a letter to Theo dated 2 July 1889 describes the cypresses, wheat, poppies, Scottish plaid-like blue sky and impasto, and the Met distinguishes this summer painted-on-site work from 2 September indoor renditions. National Gallery of London identifies its September version as painted indoors from the earlier study. The letter is a first-person description in 1889, not proof of a claimed feeling of awe.
